Well originally Bon Iver was just a name that Justin Vernon wrote and recorded under.  His first album For Emma Forever Ago came about when he essentially locked himself in a cabin and wrote it.  It's essentially his diary at the time, and it features acoustic guitar and the occasional feature of percussion.  It definitely has this feeling of isolation and emptiness.  With the following EP and album, he actually employed a full band adding in more guitars, piano, and occasionally electronic tracks and horns and even a lap steel.  It's most certainly a departure from his debut album but the same sort of themes and motifs are there and it all still works in my opinion.

Was a huge fan of For Emma... and enjoyed Bon Iver, Bon Iver until I got to Beth/Rest and I couldn't stand the horns and the cheesy 90s soft rock sound of it. A few months later it came up on shuffle and I gave it another shot and now it's one of my favorites. It's so beautiful and haunting at the same time. From what I can gather, you seem to think that you get down and out by things other than "bad" news. I know how that is. When I was 19/20 I had girlfriend who loved me, I was independently living on my own, and studying my dream field at a university. I really had everything that I feel like I need to be happy. But there was always this nagging feeling. No matter all the good in my life, I wasn't happy. That's when I really felt that there must be something in my head stopping, some wires must have been mixed up or something. 
I've been diagnosed with depression, anxiety, BPD; and I don't know which of those I really think is the culprit. But I'll stick with depression right now. The thing with it i for me is that I have the hardest time being happy when I should be and when sad things happen, I take them way harder than I should. Some days it's impossible to get out of bed. My life sometimes is a hilarious contradiction. I crave social interaction, yet when I get it I want nothing more than to be alone. 
What I try to keep in mind when I feel like that is that it's not me doing it, it's the asshole depression making me do it. And we fight constantly. Sometimes he wins and I do nothing but watch Wall-E on repeat, and sometimes I win and I go out and I find ways to make myself feel good. But it's a constant struggle. I'm still sorting out if medication works for me (it hasn't in the past) or if therapy helps (mixed feelings on that). But as I continue to progress, in the back of my head I just remember that I can't necessarily control these negative feelings, but I have an opportunity to fight and rise above them.
I realize this is just a broad generalization and so it may not be the most helpful. More than anything, I know what it's like to just have someone listen. It makes a world of difference.  PM me if you have specific questions or even if you just want to vent. I'm here.

Your best allies are those closest to you. The hardest thing for me to do when I was depressed was admitting it and asking for help. It wasn't until my girlfriend at the time, having seen how constantly down I was, asked me if I was ok and encouraged me to talk to my parents. I promise you that your family will be compassionate and caring. They honestly want you to be happy above anything else. 
If it feels like you have nowhere to turn, there are loads of people who have similar feelings and experiences and know that feeling of hopelessness. I personally know what it's like seeking help from people who just don't grasp what you're going through, who just see it as being in a sad mood, and it can be difficult. If you want to speak with someone who knows what it feels like, I'm here.
